name: Webhook retry: an endpoint that is down, and nothing lost
description: The city's curb platform subscribes to Lakeside's device events, then its endpoint goes down. An exit-gate fault is published; the simulated receiver answers 500, 500, then 200, and the delivery ledger shows each attempt on the Part 8 schedule (0 s, 30 s, 2 min) until the event is delivered, the same envelope every time, re-signed per attempt. Then the city pauses its subscription for a deploy: an event published meanwhile is held and delivered on resume.

steps.name: Lakeside Garage, 18:00 on a Thursday
steps.narration: The city's curb platform wants to know when Lakeside's lane equipment changes state. APX delivers events as signed webhooks with a fixed retry schedule, so a subscriber that is briefly unreachable still gets every event. The simulated clock is frozen at 18:00 and moves only when a step moves it.

steps.name: The city subscribes to device state
steps.narration: A webhook subscription at APDS's own /webhooks route. Asking for the representation returns the subscription and its signing secret, once; the server will not disclose the secret again.

steps.name: The city's endpoint goes down
steps.narration: The simulator stands in for the city's server. It is told to answer the next two deliveries with 500 and the third with 200, as an endpoint would during a short outage.

steps.name: 18:14: the exit barrier faults
steps.narration: The arm sensor on exit lane 2 reports a fault. The PARCS publishes apx.control.device.state.v1, and the first delivery attempt goes out at once.

steps.name: First attempt: 500
steps.narration: The delivery ledger is part of the standard, not a simulator feature: the subscriber can read it at GET /webhooks/{id}/deliveries. One attempt, code 500, status retrying.

steps.name: 18:14:29: the retry is due, not yet sent
steps.narration: Part 8 fixes the delays between attempts: 30 seconds, then 2 minutes, 10 minutes, 1 hour, then hourly for 24 hours. Twenty-nine seconds on, the ledger still shows one attempt.

steps.name: 18:14:30: second attempt, 500 again
steps.narration: Thirty seconds after the first attempt the server tries again. Still down; the next try is scheduled two minutes later.

steps.name: 18:16:30: third attempt, delivered
steps.narration: The endpoint is back and answers 200. The ledger records the event as delivered after three attempts, with the time and code of each.

steps.name: What the city's server received
steps.narration: Three POSTs carrying the same event id and the same body. Each attempt has its own APX-Delivery-Id, an APX-Timestamp of that attempt, and an APX-Signature computed over that timestamp and the body, so a late retry verifies as well as the first. The receiver can de-duplicate on the event id.

steps.name: 18:30: the city pauses for a deploy
steps.narration: Planned downtime is handled by the subscriber, not by failed deliveries. The city sets its subscription to paused; the server holds events for it for up to 24 hours.

steps.name: 18:41: the barrier is repaired while paused
steps.narration: A technician clears the fault and the gate reports available. The event is published, but nothing is sent to the paused subscription and its ledger has no new record: a held event has no delivery until its first attempt.

steps.name: 18:50: the city resumes
steps.narration: Setting the subscription back to active releases what was held, in the order it was published.

steps.name: Nothing was lost
steps.narration: Two events were published while the city was unreachable or paused, and the ledger shows both delivered: the fault after three attempts, the repair on its first attempt at resume. The city's view of the gate matches the garage's.
